trials.name: Long horizon credit
trials.hypothesis: Raise gamma to 0.99 and gae_lambda to 0.95. The success signal is the +1 bonus for an exact build, given at episode end. With gamma 0.95 and lambda 0.9 it is heavily discounted at the early placements that decide exactness, such as avoiding overhangs and getting the order right. """Starting architecture: the main campaign's default policy (conv encoder, width 64, depth 2, ReLU,
no normalisation), rewritten as a candidate file. A 3x3 conv body, a 1x1 conv placement head
(one logit per brick type and anchor cell), and DONE and value heads on mean+max pooled features."""
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

WIDTH = 64
DEPTH = 2


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        layers, c_in = [], spec.in_channels
        for _ in range(DEPTH):
            layers += [nn.Conv2d(c_in, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU()]
            c_in = WIDTH
        self.body = nn.Sequential(*layers)
        self.place_head = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, spec.n_types, 1)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        place = self.place_head(f).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

analyses.1: There are no trials yet. The baseline's four seeds scored 0.068, 0.068, 0.258 and 0.068, so whether a run succeeds depends heavily on seed luck. Any gain needs to be large, roughly above 0.15 mean, before it means much. The default recipe only allows 131072 / (256*16) = 32 PPO updates, which is very few for a 401-action policy. So the number of updates is probably a bottleneck. Two other levers look worth testing. First, the +1 exact-build bonus comes at episode end, often 10 to 20 steps later, while gamma 0.95 and lambda 0.9 discount it heavily. Second, fewer PPO epochs buy more samples: 2 epochs give about 243k steps. This round tests three changes: (1) longer credit horizon, (2) many more, smaller updates, and (3) a combined recipe with more data and updates plus a long horizon.
analyses.2: All three round-1 recipes scored 0.068, the same as three of the four baseline seeds. 0.068 is about 35/512, so it looks like a common plateau: the agent solves a small set of easy designs and stops improving. The baseline's 0.258 seed shows that escaping this plateau is possible, but it happens rarely. A longer horizon, more updates and more samples at 2 epochs did not move the plateau in any seed, so the bottleneck is probably exploration or policy collapse rather than credit horizon or update count. This round tests the entropy coefficient in both directions, since the action space has about 400 actions and the bonus may be badly scaled. It also tests the largest sample budget the rules allow (1 epoch, about 426k steps) while keeping a similar number of gradient steps. The aim is to find any recipe that clears the 0.068 plateau in both seeds.
analyses.3: 0.0684 (35/512) is a fixed plateau: most runs land on exactly that score, including runs with a longer horizon, more updates, or 1.85 to 3.25 times more fresh samples. The data and horizon changes did nothing. Only entropy changes moved runs off the plateau. ent 0.03 gave seeds of 0.068 and 0.334 (mean 0.201, the best so far). ent 0.002 gave 0.123 and 0.158, smaller but both seeds escaped. The baseline escaped in 1 of 4 seeds, so all of this is within seed luck. Still, the entropy setting is the only control linked to escaping, perhaps because it changes how probability is shared between DONE and about 400 placement actions. Learning rate is untested. This round brackets the best trial: one candidate pushes entropy to the maximum, and two keep ent 0.03 and try a lower and a higher learning rate. Each result can then be read against r2c2.
analyses.4: Changing the discount horizon, the update count or the amount of fresh data did nothing at default lr and entropy: every seed sat on the 0.068 plateau. Entropy is the lever that matters. ent_coef 0.03 and 0.05 each freed at least one seed (means 0.20 and 0.22). ent_coef 0.002 also scored 0.14, but on two seeds that may be noise. Learning rate interacts strongly with entropy. At ent 0.03, lr 5e-4 collapsed both seeds to 0.068, while lr 2e-3 freed both (0.334 and 0.416, mean 0.375). The best reading is that the agent must escape an early collapse onto easy designs, and then needs enough optimisation progress within only 32 updates with a decaying learning rate. Since this is the last round, each candidate pushes one of these directions a step further: lr 3e-3, entropy 0.05, or a wider PPO clip. Any that scores above about 0.22 joins the top 3 and gets the extra seeds.
